title: Mastering Border Radius Systems
summary: This lesson teaches how to create a consistent border radius system in UI design. It covers mathematical formulas for nested corners and selection rings, scaling radius with component size, and handling edges and images.

transcript.text: Every corner rounded. Still looks off. Corners are a system.
Same radius inside and out. The inner corner bulges. Inner equals outer minus padding. 12 outside, 8 of padding, 4 inside. Now the corners are concentric.
8 pixels on everything. A chip and a modal don't share a corner. Radius follows size. Small 4, medium 8, large 16. One scale, every element on it.
Full radius isn't a number, it's a shape. A pill fits one line. Chips, avatars, toggles. On a card, the corners swallow the content. Multi-line gets a real number.
A sheet docked to the bottom. The top corners round, the bottom ones hit zero. A corner means space beyond it. Touching an edge? No corner.
A selection ring drawn as its own box, two pixels out. Inherit the radius and the corners pinch. Flip the formula: outer equals inner plus the gap. Eight in, ten out.
Edge-to-edge image in a rounded card. Its square corners poke through. Let the card clip it. Inset image? Subtract the padding. Same rule.
Follow for more UI systems. Save this before your next card.

on_screen_text: One radius everywhere is not a system
One scale, every element on it
Full radius is a shape, not a number.
A pill fits exactly one line
A corner means space beyond it
Outer equals inner plus the gap.
Let the card clip the image.
Clip it, or subtract the padding
design_principles: Pill shapes for single-line elements only
Zero radius for edges touching screen borders
Outer ring radius = inner radius + gap
Clip images or subtract padding for inset images
before_after: The video demonstrates the transformation from a visually inconsistent UI using a single border radius to a harmonious system where radii are calculated based on nesting, size, and context.
